what_its_for: Lactic acid is a moisturizer used to treat dry, rough, scaly, or flaky skin. It helps soften and smooth the skin by helping your skin hold onto moisture and gently removing dead skin cells. It is also used for conditions like keratosis pilaris (small bumps on the skin), ichthyosis (very dry, scaly skin), and other rough skin problems.
how_to_take: Lactic acid comes as a cream, lotion, or solution that you apply directly to your skin. Clean and dry the affected skin area first. Apply a thin layer of the product and gently rub it in. Wash your hands after applying unless you are treating your hands. Avoid getting it in your eyes, nose, mouth, or on broken or irritated skin. If it does get in your eyes, rinse thoroughly with water.
dosing: Apply to the affected skin area 1 to 2 times per day, or exactly as directed by your doctor or as stated on the product label. Do not use more than recommended. The strength of lactic acid products varies (usually 5% to 12%), so always follow the instructions for the specific product you are using.
missed_dose: If you forget to apply a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply extra to make up for a missed application.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep the container tightly closed when not in use. Keep away from heat and direct sunlight. Do not freeze. Keep out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting lactic acid in your eyes, inside your nose, or in your mouth. Avoid applying to cuts, scrapes, open wounds, or severely broken skin. Avoid using on skin that is already very irritated or inflamed. Some people experience increased sun sensitivity, so try to limit sun exposure on treated areas, wear protective clothing, and use sunscreen when going outside. Avoid using other harsh skin products on the same area at the same time unless your doctor approves.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor if you experience: severe burning, stinging, redness, or irritation that does not go away after a few days of use; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, swelling, severe itching, or trouble breathing; skin that appears to be getting worse instead of better; or any unusual skin changes. Mild stinging or tingling when you first apply the product is common and usually goes away as your skin gets used to it.
when_it_works: You may start to notice your skin feeling softer and smoother within a few days to 1 to 2 weeks of regular use. For best results, continue using it as directed even after your skin improves. Full improvement for rough or scaly skin conditions may take 4 to 6 weeks or longer with consistent use.
special_populations: Children: Lactic acid is generally not recommended for use on children under 2 years of age unless directed by a doctor. Use carefully on children and keep away from their face. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before using this product. Topical use is generally considered low risk, but always check with your healthcare provider first. Elderly: Older adults may have more sensitive skin, so watch for extra irritation and start with less frequent application if needed.
